title: Gen-CE
fill_note: DENSE layered wind with a jig; scorer cap 0.65
fill_how: The scored turns assume a dense, layer-by-layer wind at fill 0.65 (insulated-wire area / window; the scorer cap). Use a winding jig on a drill/lathe with a turn counter, lay each layer side-by-side with light back-tension, and do not scramble-wind: a scramble wind only reaches ≈0.55–0.60 and then the window holds fewer turns (scorer what-if `--fill 0.60` is in the table above). Never wind more than the listed turns — the copper must stay below the flanges.
steel_extra: **New steel:** Ø198 discs, M3 clamp map R30 at 0/90/180/270° and R44 on the inter-pole angles 67.5/112.5/247.5/292.5° (both inside the R86 magnet ring). Cut from this kit's `steel_backiron_disc.dxf`; no earlier disc fits.
o5_note: scan t6: diametric Ø5 assists lower this 8p/12c layout, so all 48 Ø5 are left out
card_title: Gen-CE · Gen-CD rotors · MIN-GAP wire-saver stator (≈300 m)
card_sub: same R86 arcs / hubs / Ø198 steel / bridges as Gen-CD · 12 bobbins r64–104 × 3.9 mm copper (gap ≈6.5 mm) · no Ø5 · 2026-10-14
idea: Wire-saver stator for the Gen-CD rotors: only 3.9 mm of copper (≈9 layers), magnet faces ≈6.5 mm apart, peak Bz ≈0.70 T. Uses ≈300 m of wire (≈80 m less than Gen-CD) and still clears Gen-BX; shares every rotor part, the steel, the frame rods and the bearing bridges with Gen-CD, so the two stators swap on the same machine.
halb_block:
halbach_magnetisation = "none";  // NO O5 assist magnets in this kit (scan: they lower the 4-pole score)
rotor_b_same_axis   = true;     // same-index magnets share one axis: N faces S across the gap
